National Policy Statement electricity networks EN-5 2025
Electricity Network Connections Designated Strategic Plans Regulations 2026

official_measurement_examples.name: EN-5 current policy
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2025 electricity networks National Policy Statement came into force on 6 January 2026 for nationally significant electricity network infrastructure; it is policy context, not a connection offer or parcel planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Land-right requirement
official_measurement_examples.fact: EN-5 states network applicants need ownership, sufficient land rights such as easements, or permission such as wayleaves; network need alone does not create parcel access rights.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 reform response status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The government response updated 27 April 2026 contains reforms requiring later legislation or secondary rules in some areas, so proposed necessary-wayleave changes must not be treated as already universally operative.

official_measurement_examples.name: Connections queue reform
official_measurement_examples.fact: Ofgem's 16 June 2026 demand-connections update describes a large queue and reform work; queue position or reform eligibility is not a firm energisation date or guaranteed network capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 37 distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 37 consent applies to specified overhead electric lines and is distinct from planning permission, land rights, connection agreements and other environmental consents.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current Section 37 example
official_measurement_examples.fact: A 21 May 2026 screening decision concerned replacement of 11kV poles and Section 37 consent; an individual screening or consent decision is project-specific and not parcel-wide precedent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Wayleave versus ownership
official_measurement_examples.fact: A wayleave or easement grants defined rights or permissions and must not be interpreted as freehold ownership, unrestricted access or development capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Connection versus planning
official_measurement_examples.fact: A network connection offer or strategic connections classification does not itself grant planning permission or prove that required substations, cables, land rights and reinforcement are delivered.

core_rules: EN-5 policy is not a connection offer
network need is not land-right evidence
reform proposal is not enacted rule until operative
queue position is not capacity guarantee
connection offer is not energisation guarantee
Section 37 consent is distinct from planning permission
Section 37 consent is distinct from land rights
easement is not unrestricted development right
strategic plan designation is not individual project approval
network reinforcement assumption is not delivered capacity
no parcel electricity-capacity clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official DESNZ, Ofgem, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. January-June 2026 EN-5, connections reform, land-rights response and Section 37 examples retained with policy, queue, capacity, land-right and planning separation; no parcel promotion.
